principles: Keep refactors behavior-preserving and split them into small prerelease increments.
Validate the applied source, not only staging scripts.
Use the built-in updater to test each completed prerelease increment.
Keep user-facing patch notes separate from engineering handoff details.

releases.title: User and account backend modularization
releases.summary: Started the backend modularization by extracting the user and account domain from dashboard.py into torrent_dashboard/users.py without intentional behavior changes.
highlights: Moved password hashing and verification, user normalization, profile editing, avatar handling, password changes, role helpers, and user CRUD into torrent_dashboard/users.py.
Preserved the existing dashboard.py call surface by importing and re-exporting the extracted helpers.
technical: Established torrent_dashboard as the package boundary for subsequent backend extraction work.
validation: Python compilation and release source validation passed before the prerelease was published.

releases.title: Serialized configuration mutations
releases.summary: Prevented lost configuration updates by moving application-generated configuration mutations onto a serialized read-modify-write transaction path.
highlights: Added torrent_dashboard/config_store.py with a shared reentrant lock.
Configuration mutations now reload the latest config while holding the lock, apply the requested transformation, atomically replace config.json, and release the lock only after the write completes.
Profile, password, avatar, user, integration, settings, update-source, notification-sound, setup, and CLI password writes use the transaction path.
fixes: Concurrent dashboard configuration writes can no longer silently overwrite unrelated changes made by another request.
technical: First-run setup rechecks setup completion inside the transaction to prevent duplicate concurrent setup commits.
Development and prerelease publication were separated into dedicated branches so intermediate commits are not exposed through the updater.
validation: Added concurrent mutation regression tests that verify two simultaneous changes both survive.
Added failed-mutation coverage to verify exceptions do not persist partial state.
known_issues: The transaction lock protects writes made by the running Torrent Dashboard process; it does not coordinate an external editor modifying config.json at the same instant.

releases.title: Release notes and project handoff pipeline
releases.summary: Adds a structured release metadata pipeline that generates GitHub release notes, in-app patch notes, a cumulative changelog, and a durable project handoff document for future development sessions.
highlights: Added release_notes/releases.json as the single source of truth for release summaries and engineering handoff context.
Added release_tools/generate_release_notes.py to generate GitHub release bodies, CHANGELOG.md, and PROJECT_STATE.md deterministically.
The Updates page now displays patch notes returned in the existing GitHub release manifest.
Prerelease publication uses the generated release body instead of a hard-coded release description.
technical: CI validates that CHANGELOG.md and PROJECT_STATE.md match the structured release metadata before publication.
Release metadata contains user-facing notes and separate engineering fields so future sessions can recover project state without relying on conversation history.
validation: The generator validates semantic versions, duplicate versions, required release summaries, and next-step structure.
JavaScript syntax checks cover the patch-note renderer, which renders release Markdown through text nodes rather than injecting release HTML.
architecture: The application remains a Python standard-library ThreadingHTTPServer service with most HTTP routing still in dashboard.py.
User and account domain logic lives in torrent_dashboard/users.py.
Configuration transaction coordination lives in torrent_dashboard/config_store.py while config normalization and migration logic still lives in dashboard.py.
The updater consumes public GitHub Releases and already exposes each release body as manifest.notes.
Completed development increments are published from prerelease/backend-modularization; active refactor work remains on refactor/backend-modularization-users.
decisions: Continue modularization in behavior-preserving increments rather than combining refactors with unrelated feature changes.
Use structured release metadata rather than commit-message inference as the authoritative source for release notes.
Keep PROJECT_STATE.md generated and read-only so it cannot drift from release metadata.

next_steps.title: Extract configuration normalization and persistence
next_steps.detail: Move config loading, migration, normalization, sanitization, and atomic persistence out of dashboard.py while preserving ConfigStore as the transaction coordinator.

next_steps.title: Expand behavioral tests
next_steps.detail: Add end-to-end authorization, account, CSRF, setup, and configuration mutation coverage around the new module boundaries.

next_steps.title: Harden secrets at rest
next_steps.detail: After the configuration module boundary is stable, add restrictive file permissions and a cleaner separation between ordinary configuration and stored credentials.
